issue.title: Unable to do helm dependency build
issue.body:
@taylorsilva I am getting an error while doing `helm dependency build`

```
➜  concourse-chart git:(release/5.7.x) helm dependency build
Error: Chart.lock is out of sync with Chart.yaml
```

Can you check ?

body:
Hi, would you use helm 3.0.1 to reproduce it? Helm 3.0.1 has solved a same problem: https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/7119.

If you can reproduced this by Helm 3.0.1, can you provide a more detailed description for reproduced it ?

I was able to reproduce this issue with helm `3.0.1`

```
┌─[/tmp/test-chart]
└─▪ helm version
version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.0.1", GitCommit:"7c22ef9ce89e0ebeb7125ba2ebf7d421f3e82ffa", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.13.4"}
┌─[/tmp/test-chart]
└─▪ helm dependency build
Error: Chart.lock is out of sync with Chart.yaml
```

There is no `Chart.lock` file present before of after `helm dependency build` is executed.

@taylorsilva This might also be affected by the issue fixed in #7009. Do you mind checking against the latest Helm 3 code in master to see if the issue is fixed? Can you also remove any `Chart.lock` file and check that your dependencies are defined in `requirements.yaml` only.

I was able to reproduce the issue using the latest code on master.

```
/t/test-chart $ /tmp/helm version
version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.0", GitCommit:"0fd76b2a2bca5b3febf6488c860a7c6502c70086", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.13.4"}

/t/test-chart $ ll
total 32
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   106B Dec 16 09:39 Chart.yaml
drwxr-xr-x  3 pivotal  wheel    96B Dec 16 09:39 charts
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   240B Dec 16 09:39 requirements.lock
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   146B Dec 16 09:39 requirements.yaml
drwxr-xr-x  9 pivotal  wheel   288B Dec 16 09:39 templates
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   1.5K Dec 16 09:39 values.yaml

/t/test-chart $ /tmp/helm dependency build
Error: Chart.lock is out of sync with Chart.yaml

/t/test-chart $ ll
total 32
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   106B Dec 16 09:39 Chart.yaml
drwxr-xr-x  3 pivotal  wheel    96B Dec 16 09:39 charts
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   240B Dec 16 09:39 requirements.lock
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   146B Dec 16 09:39 requirements.yaml
drwxr-xr-x  9 pivotal  wheel   288B Dec 16 09:39 templates
-rw-r--r--  1 pivotal  wheel   1.5K Dec 16 09:39 values.yaml
```

Sanity checks:
- Still works using Helm v2
```
/t/test-chart $ helm2 dependency build
Hang tight while we grab the latest from your chart repositories...
...Successfully got an update from the "harbor" chart repository
...Successfully got an update from the "concourse" chart repository
...Successfully got an update from the "stable" chart repository
Update Complete.
Saving 1 charts
Downloading postgresql from repo https://kubernetes-charts.storage.googleapis.com/
Deleting outdated charts
```
- There's no `Chart.lock` file before or after running any of the `dependency build` commands
- Contents of `requirements.yaml` has not changed before or after running any of the `dependency build` commands
@taylorsilva Thanks for helping in reproducing the issue. I'm able to see the bug following the steps. @hickeyma I think we need to label this as `bug`.

I was able to reproduce this as well with the latest build
```
$ helm fetch stable/wordpress --untar
$ helm dependency build wordpress/
Error: Chart.lock is out of sync with Chart.yaml
```

issue.title: fix(chart): lock digest differs when dependency build with Helm 2 and then Helm 3

issue.body:
When apiVersion v1 chart dependencies are built with Helm 2 and then built with Helm 3, the lock digests differ. To avoid this issue, a dependency update is forced.

Fixes #7233

body:
Sorry for the delay in replying but got side tracked before I could reply with my investigations.

@taylorsilva Thanks for testing the issue against the latest code.

I have been looking at the issue and trying to work out the best way to handle it. As it stands the logic is working as expected. The issue is happening because when apiVersion v1 chart dependencies are built with Helm 2 and then built with Helm 3, the lock digests differ.  This is to be expected as different code builds the digest in the Helm 2 and 3 cases.

Should the logic remain as is or should it realign in code. @waveywaves I am not sure if you were working on this but I hope it is ok that I pushed PR #7261 as a possible solution that I had already ready.

rename.from: [Helm3] Chart.lock is out of sync with Chart.yaml for Charts using API v1
rename.to: Lock digest differs when performing dependency build on chart in Helm 2 and then Helm 3

body:
I assume the root cause for this issue was the change in hashing mechanism introduced to fix #2731?

Perhaps the API-stablest approach would be to teach `HashReq` to generate the right kind of hash depending on the chart version?

However, that would reintroduce #2731 into APIVersionV1 charts in Helm v3, so it might be better to treat those older hashes as legacy. They would be accepted during `helm dep build` or similar validations, but never *generated* by Helm v3.

That in-turn might introduce issues for Helm v2 validating APIVersionV1 charts generated by Helm v3. Which would be a real shame, getting the fix for #2731 was a driver for my site upgrading to Helm v3 pretty much the week it was released.

Is `helm dep build` the only thing that actually validates this hash? We locally commit our charts as well as the lockfile, so we never use `helm dep build`, and so would never have noticed this issue ourselves, but it's only because we have `skipDependenciesBuild` turned off in our skaffold.yaml for historical reasons.

Would you even need to download everything again? It just needs to update the digest against the right structure based on the input. The algorithm didn't change, it just went from hashing the requirements, to hashing the requirements+lock (#5874 + #6736). I don't see any recursion or walking for sub-charts involved here, and my _recollection_ is that the `chart.Dependency` structure didn't change particularly in the Helm v2->v3 change, when I went looking previously.
